claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi has coercivity of approximately 100 Oe or less.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Ti and applying the proposed heat treatment will induce Ti-rich precipitation in FCC FeCoNi.
The resulting Ti-rich precipitates will be uniformly dispersed, nanometer-scale, and coherent with the FCC FeCoNi matrix.
Solution annealing near 1100°C followed by aging near 500°C for 1–5 hours will produce the desired precipitate structure.
Coherent Ti-rich precipitates will pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning by the precipitates will increase the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The intervention will increase coercivity well above the approximately 100 Oe baseline.
The intervention will retain high saturation magnetization without a significant reduction.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during processing.
The intervention is effective only when precipitate formation is tightly controlled by the specified heat treatment.
The precipitation approach is applicable to bulk FeCoNi-based samples with approximately 2 at.% Ti.
The coercivity increase will depend on precipitate size and distribution.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis proposes nanometer-scale coherent precipitates as effective domain-wall pinning centers, whereas the cited introduction states that precipitates only a few nanometers in size, below the domain-wall thickness, do not interact with Bloch walls. The cited abstract likewise reports that a high volume fraction of coherent precipitates below 15 nm increased coercivity only marginally, to less than 10.7 Oe.
